chapter: Learning the trombone and jam sessions
title: Why playing with unfamiliar musicians matters
summary: Playing with new people changes your ideas; he enjoys playing swing alongside modern trombonists.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: But, you know, like when you're jamming -- a jam session, if you really -- your true thing comes out when you're playing with people you haven't been playing with because it makes you play a little bit different. You play -- you don't notice it but really you can get a -- get in a rut playing with the same guy all the time. When you're playing with somebody different your ideas become a little different because they're playing a little different way. This is what I find anyway in my playing, you know.

Yeah, you would. I find it to be true. But naturally, if you -- most guys, if they're going to do something real important you like to have a guy that know what you're doing. But when you're with pros -- when you're with the real pros, they can do what you're doing. They might have a little different twist to the way they do it, you know.

I find it real challenging -- I find it real challenging to really play with guys that you haven't been playing with all the time. And when I play with guys like Waters, and Watrous Rosalino, you know, and them, well,

they play altogether different from what I play. You know, my style is more the swing style and they're real up on top of the modern thing. And I enjoy what they're doing. And, of course, it doesn't make me change my way of playing. It's just the contrast in the playing, you know. But I enjoy doing things like that. And --
